script.title: The Theater Secret: Why 'Good Luck' is a Curse
script.hook: Stop saying 'good luck' before a play. That phrase is actually bad luck.
script.setup: Most people think wishing someone luck is positive. But in theater, it's considered a total curse. It's an old insider secret.
script.discovery: The real expression is 'break a leg.' It's how professionals wish each other success backstage. It's the vibe you need.
script.example: Before my big show, I told my friend, 'Break a leg tonight, you'll crush it.' It sounds way more natural.
script.payoff: Hearing 'break a leg' instantly shows you know the real vibe. What would you say instead? Drop your version below!
